M1.name: Zero velocity, zero acceleration
M1.belief: If it stops for an instant, nothing is accelerating it.
M1.truth: Acceleration can be non-zero while velocity is zero, as at the top of a vertical throw.

M2.name: Sign means slowing
M2.belief: Negative acceleration always means slowing down.
M2.truth: Speeding up or slowing down depends on whether acceleration and velocity point the same way.

M3.name: Acceleration follows motion
M3.belief: Acceleration always points the way the object moves.
M3.truth: Acceleration points the way velocity is changing; gravity always points down.

M4.name: Graph as picture
M4.belief: A graph shows the path or hill the object travels on.
M4.truth: A graph shows how one quantity changes with time.

M5.name: Wrong graph feature
M5.belief: Reads height when slope or area is needed, or reads a v-t graph as x-t.
M5.truth: Slope of x-t is velocity, slope of v-t is acceleration, area under v-t is displacement.

M6.name: Distance equals displacement
M6.belief: Distance and displacement, or speed and velocity, are the same.
M6.truth: Displacement and velocity depend on direction and on the start-to-end change.

M7.name: Average of speeds
M7.belief: Average speed is the mean of the two speeds.
M7.truth: Average speed = total distance / total time; a simple mean works only when the times are equal.

M8.name: Heavier falls faster
M8.belief: Heavier objects fall faster when there is no air resistance.
M8.truth: Without air resistance, all objects fall with the same acceleration.

M9.name: Horizontal speed changes fall time
M9.belief: A faster horizontal launch takes longer or shorter to land.
M9.truth: Horizontal and vertical motion are independent; fall time depends only on height.

M10.name: Stopped at the top
M10.belief: A projectile's velocity is zero at its highest point.
M10.truth: Only the vertical component is zero; the horizontal component remains.

Q1.stem: A ball is thrown straight up at 20 m/s. Find its velocity and acceleration 2 s after it is thrown.
options: Velocity 10 m/s upward, acceleration 10 m/s² downward

Q2.stem: A trolley rolls up a smooth ramp at 6 m/s. It slows at a constant 3 m/s² and stops for an instant at t = 2 s. What is its acceleration at that instant?
options: Zero, because it is not moving

Q3.stem: Taking upward as positive, a stone is dropped from a tall tower, so its acceleration is −10 m/s². Its velocity is −10 m/s at t = 1 s and −30 m/s at t = 3 s. Between these times the stone is:
options: Speeding up, from 10 m/s to 30 m/s
Slowing down, because its acceleration is negative
Slowing down, because its velocity fell from −10 to −30
Moving at constant speed, because its acceleration is constant

Q4.stem: A car moves in the −x direction with velocity −20 m/s and a constant acceleration of −2 m/s². What is its speed after 5 s?
options: 10 m/s, the negative acceleration slowed it
30 m/s, but it has slowed down since −30 is less than −20

Q5.stem: A ball is thrown straight up at 15 m/s. At t = 1 s it is still rising. Find its velocity and acceleration at that moment.

Q6.stem: A cyclist moving east at 12 m/s brakes evenly and stops in 4 s. During braking, the acceleration is:
options: 3 m/s² east, the way she is moving
Zero, because she ends at rest

Q7.stem: The position-time graph of a car on a straight road is shown. Between t = 6 s and t = 10 s, the car:
options: Moves back toward its start at 5 m/s
Drives down the far side of a hill
Slows down, because the graph goes down
Moves back toward its start at 4 m/s

Q8.stem: The velocity-time graph of a cyclist is shown. What happens between t = 4 s and t = 8 s?
options: She rides back toward where she started
She slows down at 1.25 m/s² and stops
She slows down at 2.5 m/s² and stops

Q9.stem: The velocity-time graph of a car starting from rest is shown. How far does it travel in the first 6 s?

Q10.stem: The position-time graph of a toy car is shown. What is its velocity?

Q11.stem: A student walks 30 m east and then 40 m north, taking 50 s in total. Find her average speed and the size of her average velocity.

Q12.stem: A ball is dropped from 5 m, bounces, and rises to 3.2 m. From release to the top of the bounce, find the distance travelled and the displacement.

Q13.stem: A bus covers the first 60 km of a trip at 30 km/h and the next 60 km at 60 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole trip?

Q14.stem: A cyclist rides up a hill at 4 m/s and comes back down the same road at 12 m/s. What is her average speed for the round trip?
options: 0 m/s, because she ends where she started

Q15.stem: A 1 kg ball and a 5 kg ball are dropped together from 45 m. Ignore air resistance. When does each land?
options: The 5 kg ball lands first, after 0.6 s
The 1 kg ball takes 3 s and the 5 kg ball about 1.3 s

Q16.stem: On the Moon (no air, g = 1.6 m/s²), an astronaut drops a hammer and a feather together from 1.8 m. What happens?
options: The hammer lands well before the feather
The hammer lands first, but only slightly, since there is no air

Q17.stem: From a 20 m cliff, ball A is dropped and ball B is thrown horizontally at 15 m/s at the same moment. Ignore air resistance. Which is right?
options: B lands later, because it has further to travel
B lands sooner, because it is moving faster
Both land after 2 s, and B lands 30 m from the base
Both land after 2 s, and B lands 15 m from the base

Q18.stem: A bullet is fired horizontally at 400 m/s from 1.25 m above flat ground, and another is dropped from the same height at the same moment. Ignore air resistance. Which is right?
options: The fired bullet stays in the air much longer
Both land after 0.5 s; the fired one lands 200 m away
The fired bullet flies straight until it slows down, then falls
Both land after 0.5 s; the fired one lands 400 m away

Q19.stem: A football is kicked at 20 m/s at 30° above the horizontal. Ignore air resistance. What is its speed at the highest point?
options: 0 m/s, it stops at the top
20 m/s, the speed does not change

Q20.stem: A stone is thrown with a horizontal velocity of 12 m/s and an upward velocity of 16 m/s. At the top of its path, its velocity and acceleration are:

Q21.stem: A lift moving up at 4 m/s slows evenly, stops after 2 s, and then starts moving down. At the instant it stops, its acceleration is:
options: Zero, because it is not moving

Q22.stem: Taking right as positive, a scooter moving left at 8 m/s has an acceleration of −3 m/s². What is its speed after 2 s?
options: 2 m/s, the negative acceleration slowed it
14 m/s, but it has slowed down since −14 is less than −8

Q23.stem: A car moving north at 20 m/s slows evenly to 8 m/s in 3 s. Its acceleration is:
options: 4 m/s² north, the way it is moving
Zero, because it is still moving north

Q24.stem: The velocity-time graph of a sprinter is shown. Between t = 4 s and t = 8 s, the sprinter:
options: Runs along a flat stretch of ground
Stands still, because the line is flat

Q25.stem: The velocity-time graph of a motorbike starting from rest is shown. What is its acceleration?

Q26.stem: A car drives 3 km east and then 3 km back west to where it started, taking 10 minutes in total. Find its average speed and average velocity.

Q27.stem: A train covers 120 km at 40 km/h and then another 120 km at 120 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole journey?

Q28.stem: A 0.16 kg cricket ball and a 7 kg shot put are dropped together from 80 m. Ignore air resistance. When does each land?
options: The shot put lands first, well ahead of the ball
The shot put lands first, but only just

Q29.stem: Two marbles roll off a table 0.8 m high at the same moment, one at 1 m/s and one at 3 m/s. Ignore air resistance. Which is right?
options: The faster marble takes longer to land
Both land after 0.4 s, 0.4 m and 1.2 m from the table
Both land after 0.4 s, 1 m and 3 m from the table

Q30.stem: A ball is thrown at 30 m/s at an angle where cos θ = 0.6 and sin θ = 0.8. Ignore air resistance. What is its speed at the highest point?
options: 0 m/s, it stops at the top
30 m/s, the speed does not change

foundations.title: Foundations: describing motion
foundations.intro: Five ideas that almost every kinematics question depends on. Same conventions: g = 10 m/s^2 and no air resistance. This block is written and checked by the team, not by the model.

concepts.name: Position and axes
concepts.explain: Position is where an object is, measured from a chosen zero point (the origin) along a direction we call positive. Without a zero and a positive direction, a position has no meaning.
concepts.example: An auto-rickshaw 2 km east of the bus stand has position +2 km if east is positive, and -2 km if west is positive.

check.stem: A lift is 3 m above the ground floor. If the ground floor is zero and upward is positive, the lift's position is:
options: It cannot be stated without its speed
check.why: Position is measured from the chosen zero along the positive direction, so it is +3 m.

concepts.name: Distance and displacement
concepts.explain: Distance is how much ground was covered and it never decreases. Displacement is the straight change from start to finish, so it can be zero even after a long walk.
concepts.example: Walking 3 m east and then 4 m north is 7 m of distance but only 5 m of displacement.

check.stem: You walk 5 m east and then 5 m west. Your distance travelled and displacement are:
check.why: You covered 10 m of ground, but you finished where you started, so the displacement is zero.

concepts.name: Speed and velocity
concepts.explain: Speed tells how fast. Velocity tells how fast and in which direction. Average velocity is displacement divided by time, so a trip that ends where it started has zero average velocity.
concepts.example: A runner who completes a 400 m lap in 80 s has an average speed of 5 m/s and an average velocity of 0 m/s.

check.stem: A car travels 60 km due east in 1 hour. Its average velocity is:
options: It cannot be found without the speed at each moment
check.why: Velocity needs a direction, so the answer is 60 km/h east.

concepts.name: Acceleration
concepts.explain: Acceleration is how quickly velocity changes, not how fast the object moves. It points the way velocity is changing, so a ball rising into the air still accelerates downward.
concepts.example: A bike braking from 10 m/s to rest in 2 s has an acceleration of -5 m/s^2 if forward is positive.

check.stem: A ball is thrown straight up. While it is still rising, its acceleration points:
options: Nowhere, because it is slowing down
check.why: Gravity is the only force acting, so the acceleration is 10 m/s^2 downward the whole time the ball is in the air.

concepts.name: Reading axes and graphs
concepts.explain: Each axis states which quantity is plotted and its unit. On a position-time graph the slope is velocity; on a velocity-time graph the slope is acceleration and the area under the line is displacement.
concepts.example: A flat line on a velocity-time graph means the velocity is constant, not that the object is at rest at the origin.

check.stem: On a velocity-time graph, the area under the line between two times gives:
check.why: Velocity multiplied by time is displacement, and on a velocity-time graph that product is the area under the line.
